title: Reverse water-gas shift reference family
objective: Optional literature-backed thermal-catalyst family for RWGS screening. These candidates are meant to compare cost pressure, route maturity, and evidence quality across low-temperature noble-metal, copper-ceria, and molybdenum-nitride directions.

balanced.label: Balanced
balanced.description: Balance catalyst cost, literature confidence, route maturity, and performance.

cost-first.label: Cost-first
cost-first.description: Bias ranking toward current catalyst cost while preserving evidence and route guardrails.

evidence-first.label: Evidence-first
evidence-first.description: Reward transparent inputs and more defensible preparation routes.

citations.label: Nature Communications 2022
citations.note: Copper-ceria route clarifying active-phase evolution and stable low-temperature RWGS behavior.

citations.label: Nature Communications 2022
citations.note: Pt-MoOx/gamma-Mo2N route targeting high low-temperature RWGS activity through metal-support cooperation.

citations.label: Nature Communications 2023
citations.note: Machine-learning-guided Pt/TiO2 catalyst design for lower-temperature RWGS optimization.

citations.label: Nature Communications 2024
citations.note: Product-driven dynamic activation of molybdenum nitride routes under RWGS conditions.

citations.label: Nature Communications 2026
citations.note: High-energy Mo2N-based catalyst route prepared through pressure processing with in situ ammonia decomposition.

citations.label: Journal of Catalysis 2006
citations.note: Goguet, Shekhtman et al.: pulse-response TAP study of the reverse water-gas shift over Pt/CeO2, distinguishing redox and associative pathways.

citations.label: Topics in Catalysis 1999
citations.note: Spencer: foundational analysis of zinc oxide's role in Cu/ZnO catalysts coupling methanol synthesis to the (reverse) water-gas shift equilibrium.

citations.label: RSC Adv. 2016
citations.note: Daza and Kuhn: comparative review of catalysts for the reverse water-gas shift reaction as a CO2 conversion route, organising by support, promoter, and active metal.

citations.label: Chem. Soc. Rev. 2011
citations.note: Wang, Wang and Liu: review of recent advances in catalytic hydrogenation of carbon dioxide, broadly covering RWGS, methanation, and methanol routes.

route_templates.name: Copper-ceria RWGS route
route_templates.route_note: Strong non-noble RWGS basis when low-temperature activity is needed without moving fully to a PGM route.

route_templates.name: Pt-TiO2 low-temperature RWGS route
route_templates.route_note: Premium low-temperature route with strong activity upside but high sensitivity to Pt exposure and low-loading execution.

route_templates.name: Mo2N high-temperature RWGS route
route_templates.route_note: Cost-pressure relief route for hotter RWGS windows, with route discipline focused on nitride formation and deactivation control.

candidates.title: Cu/CeO2 baseline
candidates.summary: Copper-ceria basis for RWGS screening when non-noble low-temperature activity matters.
decision_notes: Best fit when you want to stay on broadly traded metals and still push RWGS toward lower temperature.
Ceria handling adds some route overhead, but economics remain materially easier than Pt-led routes.

pricing.note: Live Cu feed with a mild precursor conversion markup.
2025 USGS cerium-oxide price used as a bulk oxide support/promoter proxy.

candidates.title: Pt/TiO2 premium
candidates.summary: PGM-assisted RWGS route when low-temperature CO productivity is worth a noble-metal premium.
decision_notes: Performance leader for colder RWGS operation, but the economics are dominated by Pt exposure.
Most useful as a premium benchmark or when reactor thermal limits are tight.

pricing.note: Live Pt feed with a mild precursor markup for low-loading deposition.
2025e landed duty-paid unit value of U.S. TiO2 pigment imports, $3,200/t (USGS MCS Feb 2026).

candidates.title: Mo2N high-temperature route
candidates.summary: Molybdenum-nitride route for hotter RWGS windows where non-noble economics matter more than very low-temperature activity.
decision_notes: Best cost-pressure-relief route in this family when the reactor can tolerate a hotter operating window.
Nitride formation and deactivation control are the main route risks rather than raw-material cost.

pricing.note: Live molybdenum feed with a modest precursor/nitridation markup.
2025 USGS alumina import value used as a bulk support or binder proxy.
